page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-288-lssd is a high-density, memory-optimized compute instance designed for large-scale enterprise applications, high-throughput in-memory data engines, and massive database deployments. Powered by Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz, the server delivers 288 vCPUs across 144 physical cores on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include 504 MB of L3 cache alongside advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions such as AVX-512, AMX-TILE, and AMX-INT8, supporting demanding vector computations directly on the CPU.

The system provides 2232 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU, complemented by an integrated local NVMe SSD array totaling 19296 GB distributed across 48 local disks. No dedicated GPUs are included in this instance. Network configuration includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which reflects its focus as an internal back-end cluster or enterprise node.

Benchmark data demonstrates top-tier multi-core execution and high data throughput. Multi-core stress-ng tests hit 312066.06, placing the machine in the top tier of evaluated hardware. Memory throughput tests show uncached large-block reads of 1060.25 GB/sec and writes of 411.36 GB/sec, supporting high-rate memory transfers. This capability translates directly into high-throughput operations, evidenced by Redis SET throughput reaching 390.97 million operations per second and high scores in PassMark database execution and Clang software compilation.

In terms of performance tradeoffs, single-core CPU execution sits within the middle 50 percent of benchmarked environments, and sequential LLM text generation rates remain constrained due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware. However, prompt processing speeds for smaller language models remain capable via CPU-based matrix operations. Cost efficiency is driven by physical resource consolidation, replacing sprawling distributed clusters with a single high-memory, multi-disk node. Workload suitability includes in-memory databases like Redis, massive relational databases, large-scale ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency software build environments.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-288-lssd is a high-density compute and memory instance powered by Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 288 dedicated vCPUs across 144 physical cores running at 2.3 GHz, supported by 504 MB of L3 cache and hardware extensions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. It includes 2232 GB of RAM and 19296 GB of local NVMe SSD storage across 48 drives, with zero discrete GPUs. Benchmark results position the server in the top tier for multi-threaded computation, database operations, and memory bandwidth, delivering over 1060 GB/sec uncached reads and 390.97 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread speeds are standard and AI text generation is limited without dedicated GPU acceleration, the system provides high density for resource-intensive workloads. It is suitable for large-scale in-memory databases, distributed data processing, enterprise relational database systems, and extensive CI/CD build farms.
